To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two reticulon ER-shaping proteins, RTNLBs 3 and 6, interact with PD proteins and with plasma membrane proteins.
the plasmodesmal reticulon protein RTNLB3 interacts with a subset of PD-localized proteins, and RTNLB3 is enriched at plasmodesmatal desmotubules, the ER, and the plasma membrane.

the two plasmodesma-localized reticulin family proteins, RTNL3 and RTNL6, bind to a number of proteins enriched in the plasma membrane and endoplasmic Rticulum, suggesting roles for these proteins in the regulation of the endoplasmatic Reticulum and plasmodesmatal membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the binding partners of PD-resident retinol proteins and their role in PD and ER function.
understanding the role of the ER in PD development and function and how this role is mediated by the ER-shaping protein family RTNLB.
the PD proteome and the protein-protein interactions of PD-resident proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RTNLB3/6 interact with PD proteins and proteins enriched at ER and plasma membranes.
reticulon ER-shaping proteins in primary PD are part of a PD-associated protein complex that may play roles in PD biogenesis, PD function, and PD-associated signaling.

the reticulons, in addition to their role in shaping the cortical ER, also play an important role in linking the ER to the plasma membranes and the PD, which is consistent with the hypothesis that reticulon ER-shaping proteins may play a role in PD formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RTNLB3/6 interact with PD proteins, and RTNLB3 interacts with the plasma membrane.
RTNLB3, RTNLB6 and their binding partners may play important roles at PD in the control of cell-to-cell communication and in the maintenance of cell polarity.
RTNLB3/6 are involved in PD function, and their PD localization may be a consequence of ER- and/or plasma membrane-associated interactions with other proteins that are also enriched at the PD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reticulon ER-shaping proteins, in addition, to their well-characterized role in ER modeling and membrane tension, also have a role in PD and plasma membrane function.

RTNLB ER shaping proteins are present in primary PD at a time when the ER is highly remodeled, and they interact with PD proteins and plasma membrane proteins that are involved in PD function, ER-PM connections, and ER shaping.
RTNLBs, in addition to their role in ER modeling and shaping, may play important functions in linking the endomembrane system to the plasma membrane and may play a role in PD development.
